title: The Economic Outlook and Some Comments on My Policy Communication
a_rationale: Near-term path is stated only as conditionals: inclined to hold if August inflation progress continues, and a hike may be appropriate if that improvement proves fleeting. Under the spec, conditionals are not the baseline, so preferred path and timing are not observed. Upside inflation risks are stated; activity and the labor market 'are not a large factor'. Policy is 'currently only slightly restricting aggregate demand'. He explains that reaction function explicitly.
b_rationale: Although both hold and hike are conditional on August inflation, he also says policy is only slightly restricting demand and that it may not take much inflation acceleration to nudge him into tighter policy, with labor and activity 'not a large factor'. That is treated as a mild tightening bias on the preferred path, not as an unobserved dimension. Timing is still not observed (the September meeting is the decision date, not an urgency claim). Upside inflation risks and the slightly-restrictive assessment are observed, as is the stated reaction function.

title: The Signaling Value of the Summary of Economic Projections
a_rationale: The speech is mainly about how to communicate a path. The 'three 25bp hikes / 75bp over six months' figures are introduced with 'let's assume' as an illustration, not as his baseline recommendation, so they are not scored as a preferred path. He does explain a data-dependent way of signaling a likely terminal increment. Forward path, timing, current risk balance and current restrictiveness are not observed as his own baseline.
b_rationale: The 75bp / three-hike figures are presented as an assumed illustration of communication methods ('let's assume'), not as Waller's own baseline path, and are not scored as a path. A data-dependent way of signaling a likely total increment is a reaction-function/communication observation only.

title: The Economic Outlook and Some Thoughts on Labor Market Dynamism
a_rationale: Baseline is a 25bp increase at the December meeting even if October inflation improves. A 50bp December hike is explicitly conditional on October CPI coming in like the last two prints (core CPI around 0.3 percent or higher) and is therefore not the baseline path. Tightening is needed 'sooner rather than later'. Inflation is 'the focus of my attention'. Further tightening is needed, which is scored as policy not yet tight enough. The 50bp threshold is a stated reaction-function branch.
b_rationale: His plan if things proceed as expected is +25bp in December, even if inflation improves. The 50bp option is a stated branch if October core CPI is around 0.3 percent or higher, and is not the baseline path. 'Sooner rather than later' and the December date are a strong timing signal. Inflation is the focus of attention; further tightening is needed.

title: Unwavering Dedication
a_rationale: His forecast-consistent baseline is that one further upward adjustment may be appropriate late this year. That is treated as a baseline path, not a tail scenario, though it remains conditional on the forecast. After the September hike he sees 'no need for urgency' and time to gather more information, so timing is scored as non-urgent. Employment risk has receded and the risk to price stability has increased. Current restrictiveness is not assessed in so many words.
b_rationale: The one-further-adjustment sentence is explicitly conditional on the economy evolving in line with his forecast, and he immediately adds that 'that is just my forecast'. Under the spec, conditionals are not the baseline, so preferred path is not observed. 'No need for urgency' is a clear timing observation. The risk shift (employment risk receded, price-stability risk increased) is observed. Restrictiveness is not assessed.
